title: Multiple Selection (CASE/SWITCH)
objectives: Build menu logic that compares against many constant values
Understand that the CASE structure is equivalent to a chain of nested IF/ELSE

hook.text: A menu has 5 options: "1) Pizza 2) Burger 3) Salad ...". Writing a separate IF/ELSE for each option would take forever, wouldn't it?

concept.heading: The logic of CASE (multiple selection)
concept.body: When you need to branch on many CONSTANT values a variable can take, you use a CASE structure instead of writing IF/ELSE IF over and over: CASE choice / 1: ... / 2: ... / DEFAULT: ... Each "case" is a block that runs if the variable equals that value.

concept.heading: CASE = a chain of IFs
concept.body: A CASE structure is really a shortcut: behind the scenes it is equivalent to the chain "IF choice = 1 ... ELSE IF choice = 2 ... ELSE IF choice = 3 ... ELSE ...". It just reads better when you compare against many constant values.

exercises.question: When is a CASE structure preferred over a chain of IF/ELSE?
options: When a single variable is compared with many constant values
It can only be used inside a loop

feedback.correct: Correct. CASE improves readability when you compare the same variable with many constant values.
feedback.incorrect: CASE is useful in menu-style situations where a single variable is compared with many constant values.

exercises.question: Which IF chain is the following CASE structure equivalent to? (If day = 1 it writes "Monday", if day = 2 it writes "Tuesday", otherwise it writes "Unknown")
options: IF day=1 WRITE "Monday" ELSE IF day=2 WRITE "Tuesday" ELSE WRITE "Unknown" END END
None of them, CASE has no IF equivalent

feedback.correct: Correct. Behind the scenes, CASE is an IF/ELSE chain that makes consecutive equality checks.
feedback.incorrect: A CASE structure is equivalent to an IF/ELSE chain that compares each case in turn with equality (=).

exercises.question: Put the steps of the IF chain that checks a menu choice (1-3) in the correct order.
When choice ← 2, what does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: The condition choice = 2 is TRUE in the second IF.

exercises.question: What is the DEFAULT branch in a CASE structure for?
options: It runs when no case matches
It is always the first branch to run
It runs only when there is an error

feedback.correct: Correct. DEFAULT is the "catch-all" branch that kicks in when none of the other cases match.
feedback.incorrect: The DEFAULT branch runs when none of the defined cases match.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: A CASE structure is used to compare a single variable with many ___ values.

summary: CASE reads better than an IF chain when a single variable is compared with many constant values.
Behind the scenes, CASE is an IF/ELSE chain that makes consecutive equality (=) checks.
The DEFAULT branch is the "catch-all" block that runs when no case matches.
